title: Multipartite Dense-Coding Capacity
exact_target: Determine how much information several separated receivers can decode, and whether undistillable multipartite entanglement can help.

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, UnsolvedMath, record 30000176 (OWR-785-002). Catalogue curation under CC BY 4.0; definitions and English exposition added locally.

Entanglement and Decoherence: Mathematics and Physics of Quantum Information and Computation (2005), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2005/04, pp. 185--255; official report source and mathematical context.
Official EMS Press PDF of the same Oberwolfach report; PDF pages 19--21, printed pages 203--205.
Bruss et al., Dense coding with multipartite quantum states; reference in the saved dated catalogue literature review.
Das et al., distributed dense coding with two receivers; reference in the saved dated catalogue literature review.

status_qualification: The capacity depends on whether receiver decoding is local, LOCC, or global and on the assignment of senders to receivers. The report distinguishes these protocols; the question must retain that distinction. It asks both for more-than-two-receiver capacities or bounds and for usefulness of multipartite bound entanglement.
